items.note: Sabhā-maṇḍapa pillars: carved with chain and bell, said to look Greek in style, 10 ft 5 in high; OCR damaged.
items.gloss: The beauty of the sabhā-maṇḍapa lies in its large pillars on square bases. Chain-and-bell motifs are carved on them and the pillars look Greek in style. The total height of these pillars is ten feet five inches, and the lower part is square.

items.note: Circular ceiling (vitāna) held up by śālabhañjikā figures; carving said to surpass ivory work.
items.gloss: The circular ceiling of the maṇḍapa is supported by śālabhañjikā figures. The carving of the inner part of the ceiling surpasses even ivory carving. The grace of the śālabhañjikās of the vitāna is worth seeing.

items.note: A mithuna figure in the ceiling is said to resemble one on the Konārka Sūrya temple śikhara, though smaller.
items.gloss: Among these is a mithuna figure worth seeing, quite similar to the mithuna figure carved on the śikhara of the Sūrya temple at Konārka in Orissa, though smaller in size.

items.note: The eastern mukha-maṇḍapa bears many inscriptions showing that people visited from time to time and that worship continued at the temple (pilgrim records).
items.gloss: In the eastern mukha-maṇḍapa many inscriptions are found, from which it appears that people came there from time to time and worship was carried on in the temple.

items.note: Assessment: the Udayeśvara temple may be called a religious poem written on stone.
items.gloss: The Udayeśvara temple can be called a religious poem written in stone.
